Subject: GDPR: DPA & SCC logistics — next steps

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the GDPR/DPA items we discussed: 

Summary from call:
- FinHealth confirmed GDPR applies (EU data subjects) and that you are the data controller for customer data; Redwood would act as a processor for inference requests.
- You asked about our SOC 2 status, DPA template, and which SCC module to use for cross-border transfers.

Requested items I can send this week:
1) Our SOC 2 attestation (most recent report) — we will share an access link to the report with limited visibility.
2) Redwood DPA template (we recommend starting from our v3 template; redlines welcome).
3) Short SCC guidance doc (we typically propose Module 2 when the customer is controller and Redwood is a processor, but there are cases where Module 3 applies; see attached summary).

Open questions for your legal ops team (so we can prepare the right package):
- Do you require Module 2 (processor under UK/EU transfer adequacy fallback) or are you evaluating Module 3 for a controller-to-controller arrangement?
- Any additional contractual controls or hosting/location constraints (e.g., absolute ban on US-based subprocessors)?

Proposed next steps:
- I will drop the DPA template and SCC summary into DocuSign for signature after we confirm which SCC module you prefer (target: this week).
- Rishi (cc'd) will tee up a short redline conversation with your counsel if needed.
- Please complete and return the vendor security questionnaire you started; I noticed a few fields missing around data retention and subprocessors — I attached the copy you uploaded for convenience.

Would appreciate confirmation on SCC module preference and the best contact on your side for contract redlines (Tom or external counsel?). Happy to schedule a 30-min legal sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team — looping in a short legal note before we send docs to FinHealth (keeps the thread internal):

- Confirming we should position Redwood as processor and FinHealth as controller (matches Sara's note).
- Recommended SCC module: start with Module 2 standard clauses (processor) and include an appendix that documents subprocessors and data flow. Module 3 only if FinHealth insists on controller-to-controller wording; that would need additional mapping.
- Redlines we commonly see: retention window clarity, audit rights cadence, subprocessors list and notice period, and breach notification SLA (we propose 72 hours).

I'll prepare a DPA v3 bundle: DPA document, SCC Module 2 baseline, and a short companion memo explaining the Module choices and typical redline language. Plan to upload to SharePoint and send a DocuSign package by EOD Wednesday.
